note: One-verb lesson (بسط/انبسط, then زعج/أزعج/انزعج). Many disputed rows are drill stumbles or Amal extending a right answer (masc -> fem) rather than slips. Unvoweled انت in the transcript cannot show إنتَ vs إنتِ, so pronoun-gender rows on it are unprovable. Agreed A7 (14:20) is a question about the rule, challenged.

row.why: Amal asked 'كل حدا or what's everyone?' to get an alternative to his (accepted) كل حدا; he guessed كل الناس as a question and she supplied الكل (sheet: everybody / everyone | El-kul | الكل). كل الناس is valid Arabic and she said 'Yeah' to كل حدا at 10:55, so this is Amal supplying her word (tier 0), not a wrong word or an A11 slip.

rulings.why: Real moment of Amal supplying الكل, but his كل الناس is not wrong Arabic and his كل حدا was accepted: tier 0 didn't-know, not tier 1 and not grammar A11.

row.why: Amal: 'How do I say last night? I don't think we've ever used it' and built it with him (ليل, ليلة, انبارح); he offered both orders and she settled ليلة امبارح; he said 'That's a new word we need to add'. Didn't-know, not a slip.

rulings.why: Didn't-know taught by Amal (15:31 'I don't think we've ever used it'); tier 0.

row.amal_said: This your night. One night. ... بليلتك. Yes.
row.why: 'Enjoy your night': he used ليل (night-time) + ك; Amal's prompt 'One night' is the same prompt she used at 15:42 to get ليلة from ليل, so the fix is the noun choice ليلة (-> ليلتك), not an ending rule; he fixed to ليلتك at 20:49 and she confirmed بليلتك.

rulings.why: Her prompt 'One night' targets the word ليلة vs ليل (as at 15:42), so vocab tier 2 (related form of a word he knows), not grammar A4.

Self-fix before her voice: he was searching for the adjective, said 'Oh, you wrote it. Mozaj.' reading her chat at 22:46 before Amal voiced مزعج at 22:50; 'mozuj' is a vowel stumble in Latin transcription (S4/S5). The real confusion of the two adjectives is agreed row A11 (22:59).

row.amal_said: Do you remember متعب؟ ... is tiring. Same pattern as مزعج.
row.why: Amal asked if he remembered متعب, he said No, she supplied 'tiring' (sheet: tiring | Mut3eb | متعب) and he said 'Oh, that's right'. Didn't-know, tier 0.

rulings.why: Amal supplied the meaning of a sheet word he could not recall: tier 0 didn't-know.

row.medi_said: These voices or sounds are annoying. "hadhol el swat."
row.why: Plural of صوت (sheet: sound / voice | Soat | صوت) is the broken plural أصوات; he said el-swat without the a- of the pattern and Amal recast الأصوات at once. Low because a fast 'l-aswat' could be heard as 'el swat' (dropped hamza, S4).

rulings.why: Amal voiced الأصوات right after his el-swat; the missing a- is the broken-plural pattern (A9/A9b in buckets.md), so grammar rather than vocab tier 2; low because it may be only elision.

row.amal_said: أزعجتك. See? It's easier to say أزعجتك.
row.why: Amal asked for the a- form ('How do I say he annoyed me with an a?' 29:01, then 'She annoyed you'); he gave the bare زعجتك, she recast أزعجتك and he said 'Oh, that's right'. Both forms are valid (she said so at 28:13/28:56), so it is the causative-forms card F3, not scored.

rulings.why: He did not follow the requested a- form but his form is valid Arabic (28:56 'You should learn both'), so not a lexical error; filed on the unscored F3 card.

Not an error: Amal asked generically 'How do I say don't get annoyed?'; she first echoed his تنزعج (accepting it) and then added the feminine ما تنزعجي as an extension, as she did at 36:28-36:35 (ممتاز for ما تزعجني, then ما تزعجيني). Masculine generic command is fine.

S4/S5: 'bisbat' while explaining in English is a root-letter metathesis stumble (b-s-t order) and he went on to bibsit at once; Amal's بتبسط is just her saying the word while he explains, not a correction of a form he chose.

row.medi_said: So, "inti," are you annoyed? "Inti maz'ooj min ishi?"
row.amal_said: إنت مزعوج من إشي؟ ... Oh, إنتي مزعوجة. Yes. إنتي مزعوجة من إشي؟
row.why: Feminine inti with masculine مزعوج; Amal's echo at 25:24 switched the pronoun to masculine إنت to show the mismatch, and only after it he said 'Oh, it'd be maz'ooja, right?' (25:27); she confirmed إنتي مزعوجة. Her signal came before his fix, so not a self-fix.

rulings.why: Her pointed echo (إنت مزعوج) came before his maz'ooja, so it is a prompt-then-fix A8 slip, not a self-fix.

Not an error: his az'ajtu is the right Levantine form of 'you guys annoyed him' (أزعجتوه said az3ajtú). Amal only objected to adding a 'wo' sound ('You can't say أزعجتُ، wo') and then confirmed az'ajtu (31:50 'mm-hmm. أزعجتُ'), he concluded 'So there is no H'. A pronunciation/spelling discussion (S4).

Self-fix in a restart chain: 'Baz- baz'ajni. Ana biyaz...' - he moved from baz- to biyaz- on his own before Amal spoke; her صح at 35:07 endorsed biyaz- and he finished بيزعجني. S5 restart, not a slip.

row.amal_said: Been catching you saying the instead of the ب. ... ننزعج.
row.why: Amal names a habit: she has been catching him dropping the ب- (engine lost the word she named) and they both say ننزعج as the form he uses; the present we-form needs b- (بننزعج). His line in this drill shows the b-, so the slip itself is not on the transcript - kept low as a voiced rule note that needs audio.

rulings.why: Amal voiced a named-rule correction about his habit (45:27); the exact slip is not in the transcript (transcript hole), so kept with low confidence.
Duplicate of agreed A17 (same 45:54 line): A17's right already reads ليش مختلف عن WhatsApp؟, and Amal let the whole line pass (she only answered كيف؟). One moment, one row.

S4/S5 drill stumble: he had said ما تنزعجي correctly at 48:15, then lost the ن in the n-z-ع cluster while repeating; Amal's note 'it's ززز، all of them together' is pronunciation advice, and he said ما تنزعجي again at 48:39.
